candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi, before you begin developing concepts, we’ll send over some concepts that appeal to us, though naturally we also want to see your own ideas. Please hold off on starting the concepts until we’ve got back to you. Thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi, [FREELANCER_NAME_001] attached a draft logo made using AI—we were obviously only tinkering around with chat gpt. That said, we want fresh, original ideas, which is why we posted our proposal, although we do like those colours because they fit the look and feel of the Global Dough truck. The company is called 'Global Dough', so the logo should not contain the word 'truck'. The 'truck' component is only one area of the business. Put another way, 'Global Dough', the business needing the logo, will run a mobile catering truck, sell food online, and may also sell to other caterers/kitchens. This is why the business name is simply 'Global Dough', while the strapline stays the same. Are you happy to discuss anything before accepting the offer?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Thank you for these. We like the graduated orange colour and the lines beside the strapline.

Our preferences are the 1st and 3rd one, since the font used in the 2nd one feels too plain. However, someone unfamiliar with our name might not understand that the flame in the 3rd one represents an ‘O’, even though we like it.

Perhaps the flame could sit inside an ‘O’, be reshaped to look more like an ‘O’, or be superimposed over an ‘O’. Could you test all of those suggestions?

For logo 3, could we also see how it looks with ‘dough’ made slightly larger? To make the strapline more prominent, could you either outline every letter with a thin black pencil line or slightly brighten the orange tones used in the strapline lettering? We like the global dough font because it has character, particularly the G. We wondered whether a little ‘character’ could be added to a couple of the other letters, but thought it would be better to handle the revisions one stage at a time, as the existing font may be okay. Thank you—we’re moving in the right direction.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Hi, apologies for taking so long to respond.

Matt prefers number 4, where the strapline matches the colour of ‘global’ and both use graduated colours.

I was wondering, though, whether you could add a little more character to the ‘global dough’ font. The food will be genuinely authentic and freshly cooked, featuring flavours from around the world. I like the unusual shape of the ‘G’ in both words; could a similar treatment be applied to more letters without taking it too far? thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Hi, thanks for these. We’re nearly there!
1\. For the second logo, please reduce the size of the U and the H so they match the height of all the other letters in ‘ DOUGH’.
2\. Could you flip the top on the right hand side of the H in DOUGH, making it mirror the top of the U in DOUGH?
3\. Lastly, could you apply the same feature to the top of the D in DOUGH, similar to the top of the B in GLOBAL?
Please refer to the attached annotated screenshot.
After that, we’ll review it again and hopefully it will retain the ‘clean’ appearance while also having the character.
Many thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Hi, oops—I thought I had already replied!

We’d like to proceed with the agreed final version shown above, rev4-02. Thank you!

Am I correct in assuming that the logo will be supplied both with and without the black box, since a black box will not be suitable for every use?

Will we also receive every colour variant you’ve presented?

That said, I believe the primary logo should be the version in the top row of the final design: graduated orange ‘global’, black ‘dough’, and the strapline in graduated orange.

What we now need is the logo guidelines and every file type required for use online, on social media, on the truck itself, and across other hard copy materials, eg pull up banners, printed menus, uniform, etc.

Given that the files will have large file sizes, how will you share them? Wetransfer?

Thank you, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Hi, did you receive the first $75, and has the second $75 been released? I’m uncertain whether [FREELANCER_NAME_001] completed everything necessary to release the second amount, so I’ll check again.

Perhaps guidelines isn’t the right term. Earlier in our conversation, you said, “Yes, absolutely. The fixed cost includes the brand colors and font as well, so you'll have everything needed to maintain a consistent brand identity moving forward.” That is probably what I’m referring to.

For the colour versions, we only need the three you mentioned above.

Thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi, [FREELANCER_NAME_001] only now found the time to sit down and open the files on my laptop. Unfortunately, the colour codes doc will not open because it displays an error. The jpgs and pdfs open without any problems, but I’m unable to open the AI, EPS, or PSD files. For the png files, only logo 4 opens correctly; none of the others open properly. Also, when we create the website and other materials, which font should we use? Did you use an existing font, or did you create it? If you created it, which font would complement the logo or potentially match it for uses such as some headers? Thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Thank you — could you also provide written confirmation that we own the copyright, so we can trademark the logo in due course and get all those boxes ticked?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Could you please email a draft/template certificate so that I can confirm the wording is sufficient?
